newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Shaw Wallace to liquidate debt.
newsitem.headline: India's Shaw Wallace to liquidate debt.

text.p: India's liquor maker Shaw Wallace and Co Ltd said on Saturday it plans to liquidate part of its debts as part of a restructuring plan, involving disinvestment of some of its non-core businesses.

A company statement said Shaw Wallace's board of directors met at their headquarters in Calcutta on Friday and agreed that the company's core businesses were "in a healthy shape having good future prospects too."

"As regards disposal of some non-core businesses as part of the restructuring plan, the board would safeguard the employees' interests. The board further decided to set in motion a transparent process for disinvestment in a time-bound fashion."
The statement did not specifiy the businesses to be put up for disinvestment.

"The board also recognised the need for orderly liquidation of its debts," the statement said. "The board is conscious of its liabilities towards its creditors and steps will be taken to discharge its responsibilities in the process of restructuring of the company.
"The company's audited account for the year which ended on June 30, 1996 is expected to be finalised shortly for the board's approval," the statement said.
